answer: Three-shard cipher work stops one alias from faking work. Each job is cut into 3 cipher shards for 3 unrelated aliases; no alias sees the full job. Each shard is marked with its maker cipher, so a bad shard names its maker. An alias earns only when the 3 shards combine into one result that matches the public job record within 24 hours. A false shard costs its alias eligibility for the next 3 epochs plus its reward for that epoch. Shards go out in spiral order, so the same trio rarely repeats. The nectar pool pays only for combined results, so one alias cannot drain it alone.
